grammar.title: 儿 as a colloquial suffix (erhua)
grammar.explanation: Adding 儿 (r) to certain words gives them a casual, spoken flavor typical of northern Mandarin: 那 → 那儿 ("there"), 玩 → 玩儿 ("to play"), 女孩 → 女孩儿 ("girl"). It's written as its own character but pronounced fused onto the syllable before it, and doesn't change the core meaning.

grammar.title: 一点儿 for "a little"
grammar.explanation: 一点儿 (yìdiǎnr) means "a little" or "a bit". After an adjective, it softens a comparison or request: 慢一点儿 ("a little slower"), 大一点儿 ("a bit bigger"). After a verb like 要 or 会, it just means a small amount.

sentences.en: I know a little of it.
This one is a bit bigger.
